top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B038) is the most clearly bounded discovery on the slate. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work changed trade analysis from countries and industries to heterogeneous firms. They supplied a selection and reallocation mechanism and a distinct channel for gains from trade. More than twenty years of tests on customs and production microdata support the mechanism, though the welfare magnitudes depend on elasticity assumptions, so the citation should name the mechanism and not a size. Firm selection is separable from the scale-economies and location results recognised in 2008. The two-name credit set matches the model and the wider firm-level agenda without a contestable choice among names. The main residual risk is that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, and a mechanism-focused citation reduces but does not remove it. I rank P004 (Kiyotaki and Moore) second because its attribution is the cleanest, although direct identification of the collateral channel is weaker. I rank P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) third. It is a mature and very influential contribution, but its three-name credit depends on how the discovery is defined, and survival of the framework does not confirm the specific credited building blocks. P003 follows because its boundary between the task framework and the trade-shock evidence is unsettled and its estimates remain contested. A defensible award is preferable to no award, so P000 is last. This ranking rests on common criteria and not on support counts.
recusal_note: No tie to Melitz, Helpman or Redding is apparent from the profile. I disclose long-running collaboration with Klenow, Aghion, Bergeaud and Li, who are not credited in any slate proposal. I am a frequent co-author of Per Krusell (secretary) and a co-author of John Hassler (chair), and an IIES colleague of both. Both support P002, which I rank third, and I treat their arguments as evidence only. My macroeconomics, growth and firm-dynamics field is adjacent to P001, which may bias my weighting. I also co-authored the Ekonomisk Debatt summaries of the 2024 and 2025 prizes. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
